name: Nhat Tru Pagoda
summary: Walk 300 m north of the Le temple to the pagoda that keeps the pillar dated 995. The hall is a chữ Đinh plan, five front bays and three rear bays, in thôn Yên Thành, xã Trường Yên. The national ranking is 1998. The pillar became a national treasure on 25 December 2015.

notice.title: The temple ticket does not name this pagoda
notice.body: The Hoa Lu line is 20,000 đồng for an adult at the Dinh and Le temples. That line does not include chùa Nhất Trụ, about 300 m north of the Le temple.

body: The pagoda stands in thôn Yên Thành, xã Trường Yên, about 300 m north of the temple of Lê Đại Hành, in the old capital. The pillar in the court is dated 995, under Lê Đại Hành, carved with a sutra and verses. The three characters on the gate are Nhất Trụ tự, which is why the folk name is chùa Một Cột. The hall is a chữ Đinh plan: five bays in front, three bays in the upper hall, tiled in northern tiles. The upper hall's carpentry is Lê, and the front hall's woodwork is Nguyễn. The Ministry of Culture and Information ranked the pagoda a national historic and cultural relic in 1998.

Decision 2382/QĐ-TTg of 25 December 2015 named the stone scripture pillar a national treasure. The pillar has six fitted parts: a square base, a round plinth, an eight-sided shaft, an eight-sided capital, and a gourd finial, standing west of the hall. The court is over 3,000 square metres. A peace ceremony falls on the 15th of the first lunar month. Walk the gate, the court, and the pillar.

figures.caption: The court and the hall, with the karst behind
figures.alt: The tiled court and wooden hall of Nhat Tru Pagoda, with a limestone peak behind

gettingThere: Walk from the Le temple, about 300 m north, in thôn Yên Thành, xã Trường Yên. From Ga Ninh Bình, ride to the old capital first.

legs.heading: From Ga Ninh Bình
legs.body: Ride to xã Trường Yên, then walk from the temples.
